sentences.text: The instant writ petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking a direction for setting aside and quashing the notice bearing No.KRA.29/2021/01 dated 16.09.2021 issued by the respondent No.3 as well as also for a direction to the respondent authorities, more particularly, to the respondent Nos.2 & 3 to release the compensation amount of Rs.78,93,750/- being the compensation for acquisition of a plot of land owned by the petitioners measuring 2 bighas 10  lechas comprised in Dag No.184 (Pt) of Patta No.803 situated at village-Majirgaon, Mouza-Ramcharani under Azara Revenue Circle in the district of Kamrup (Metro), Assam.

From a perusal of the writ petition, it reveals that various plots of land were acquisitioned under the provisions of the Assam land (Requisition & Acquisition) Act, 1964 (for short, 'the Act of 1964')

the learned Additional Senior Government Advocate further submitted that the land has been acquired under the provisions of the Act of 1964, but the compensation has been paid in terms with the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the Act of 2013').

sentences.text: In the backdrop of the above, let this Court take note of the dispute involved in the instant case.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioners who were also the named pattadars and entitled to a portion of the awarded amount have sought for a direction that the amount of Rs.78,93,750/- be released to the petitioners as the petitioners are the owners of a plot of land measuring 2 bighas 10  lechas out of the total 5 bighas of land of Dag No.184 (Pt) covered by Patta No.803.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further seen from Annexure-7 to the writ petition that various persons were issued notice thereby fixing 22.09.2021 for hearing to determine the land compensation pertaining to acquisition of the land.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: This notice has been put to challenge.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The grounds on which the said notice has been put to challenge is that the said notice had been issued Page No.# 4/5 at the behest of the respondent No.5 who had raised an objection and that the respondent No.5 has no right to receive any amount for which the said notice dated 16.09.2021 is liable to be set aside and quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5. Therefore, from the above dispute, it would be seen that the dispute falls within the ambit of the apportionment of the compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
This Court finds it relevant to take note of Section 12 of the Act of 1964. Section 12, being relevant, is reproduced herein under:-
"12. Reference to Court.-(1) The Collector shall in every case- (a) where any person aggrieved by an award made under sub-section (3) of Section 11 makes an application requiring the matter to be referred to the Court ; or (b) where there is any disagreement with regard to the compensation payable under Sub-section (4) of Section 11 on the application of the person entitled to compensation requiring the matter to be referred to Court
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: , refer the matter to the decision of the Court .
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
(2) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Act provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, shall 1894 (Act I of 1894), shall mutatis mutandis apply in respect of any Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72290489/
3 reference made to the Court under sub-section (1)."
6.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Act, 1894, shall 1894 (Act I of 1894)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: From a perusal of the above Section, it would show that the Collector shall in every case where any person is aggrieved by an award made under Sub-Section (3) of Section 11 of the Act of 1964 or whether there is an disagreement with regard to the compensation payable on the application of the person entitled to compensation requiring the matter to be referred to Court, refer the matter to the decision of the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Sub-Section (2) of Section 12 is further of relevance in as much as the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 are made applicable in respect of any reference made to the Court under Sub- Section (1) of Section 12 of the Act of 1964, meaning thereby the provisions of Section 18 as well as Section 30 shall also apply on the basis of Legislation by incorporation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, it was the bounden duty of the Collector that if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the said amount or any part thereof or as to the person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the Collector may refer such dispute to the decision Page No.# 5/5 of the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: This Court further finds it relevant also to take note of Section 31 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894 wherein also it has been mentioned that if there is a dispute as to the entitlement to receive the compensation or as to the apportionment of it, the Collector shall deposit the amount of compensation in the Court to which a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894 would be submitted.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the dispute in the instant case as to who would be entitle the amount of Rs.78,93,750/- if cannot be settled by the Collector, the Collector or the Land Acquisition Officer so authorized has to refer the dispute to the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7. Under such circumstances, it is the opinion of this Court that the said dispute so raised in the instant writ petition cannot be decided by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
However, taking into account the provision of Section 12 of the Act of 1964 read with Sections 18, 30 & 31 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894,
this Court gives liberty to the parties, if they have any dispute as regards the apportionment of the amount to file appropriate application before the Collector or the Land Acquisition Officer so entrusted with the acquisition proceedings pertaining to LA Case No.4/2018 thereby seeking a reference to the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8. This Court further observes and directs, if such application is filed, the Collector and/or the Land Acquisition Officer, without any delay, shall refer the dispute to the Court for deciding the said dispute pertaining to apportionment.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further observed and directed that if disputes as regards apportionment cannot be resolved, the Collector/Land Acquisition Officer shall deposit the said amount in the Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. With the above observation and direction, the instant petition stands disposed of.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 17 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 08.11.2024 Heard Mr. A. Roshid, learned counsel for the petitioner; Ms. G. Hazarika, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue Department for the respondent no. 1; Mr. S. Baruah, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 2 & 3; and Mr. C. Baruah, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent nos. 4 & 5.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 2. The learned counsel for the parties have submitted that this is the 3 rd round of litigation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
3. The petitioner has been projecting that he constructed structures on a plot of land having 60 ft.
length and 80 ft. width at a place in Village - Agia, Part -II [Ulupara], Balijana Revenue Circle,
District - Goalpara near National Highway no. 17.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: A process of land acquisition was initiated by the State respondent authorities at the instance of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways [MoRT&H], Government of India [GoI] as the requiring authority for 4-lanning of National Highway no. 17.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: When the process of acquisition was being Page No.# 3/5 undertaken, the petitioner approached this Court by way of a writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 5060/2023 with the projection that the petitioner was in occupation of a plot of land measuring 4 Bighas 2 Kathas 8 Lessas, covered by Dag no. 663 at Village - Agia, Part -II [Ulupara], Balijana Revenue Circle.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: During the said proceedings, no land document was produced by the petitioner to show that he was the owner of the said plot of land.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
It was projected that he was in occupation of a Government plot of Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128560683/
2 land and as such, he would be entitled to compensation as a person interested.

The writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 5060/2023 came up for consideration on 01.09.2023 and the same was disposed of with a direction to the respondent authorities to verify whether the land wherein the petitioner was in occupation had been included in the Notifications issued under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956 and if the said land had been included in the Notifications under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956, then the respondent authorities would be at liberty to evict the petitioner from the said land.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It was further observed that the petitioner would be entitled to zirat compensation if there were any structures constructed by the petitioner or there were any standing crops belonging to the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. Subsequently on 22.03.2024, a notice was served upon the petitioner by the Competent Authority Land Acquisition [CALA], Goalpara, that is, the respondent no. 2 informing that the petitioner had constructed some unauthorized structures over the land covered by Dag no. 363, as mentioned hereinabove, which falls within the existing Right of Way [RoW] of the National Highway no. 17 already acquired, as per the Joint Verification Report of the Circle Officer, Balijana Revenue Circle dated 28.02.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The petitioner was informed that as his occupation of the land, already acquired,
was creating obstruction in the construction works of 4-lanning National Highway no. 17 from Agia [Nichinta] to Paikan [PKG-7] by the NHIDCL and the project is a time-bound central project, he should immediately vacate the plot of land, else, he would be evicted from the plot of land forcibly.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner had again approached before the Court by way of another writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 1858/2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Page No.# 4/5 6.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The Competent Authority Land Acquisition [CALA] who was impleaded as the respondent no. 3,
filed an affidavit in the writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 1858/2024 stating inter alia that in an enquiry conducted it was found that the petitioner would not be entitled to any compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
In the enquiry, it was revealed that the structures constructed by the petitioner in the plot of land covered by Dag no. 363, mentioned above, falls within the RoW of 21 metres [required for current work],
which was recorded already in the chitha copy as National Highway, meaning thereby, the land was already acquired for National Highway no. 17, which was earlier National Highway no. 37.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: When such facts were brought to light, the learned counsel for the petitioner made a submission on 06.09.2024, when the writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 1858/2024 was taken up for consideration, to the effect that since there were disputed questions of fact, he may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition, with a liberty to approach the competent court agitating the grievance as regards claim for zirat compensation in connection with the aforesaid plot of land.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: In view of such submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 1858/2024 was closed with the liberty to the petitioner, as prayed for.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. By this writ petition, the petitioner has sought to open up the litigation for the third occasion seeking inter alia a direction to the respondent authorities to assess the amount of zirat compensation in respect of the plot of land covered by Dag no. 363.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
When the writ petition, W.P.[C]
no. 1858/2024 was taken up for consideration on 06.09.2024, the learned counsel for the petitioner Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128560683/
3

sentences.text: submitted that since disputed questions of fact were involved, the petitioner be permitted to withdraw the writ petition with the liberty to approach the competent court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: In view of such submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the writ petition was closed with the liberty as sought for by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is, thus, clear that the competent court where the petitioner required to approach is not this Court exercising jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The very reason for which the petitioner made the prayer to approach the competent court was involvement of disputed questions of facts.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. It is well settled that a writ petition involving disputed questions of facts which require leading of evidence by the parties, is ordinarily not to be entertained.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Thus, it is clear that Page No.# 5/5 liberty granted to the petitioner vide Order dated 06.09.2024 cannot be a writ petition and as such,
this writ petition is not to be entertained.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 9. Despite order dated 06.09.2024, the petitioner has approached again without approaching the competent court of law.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-5 vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 8 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Such an approach is clearly an abuse of the process and as such, the petitioner is imposed with a cost of Rs. 2,000/-, which sum is to be deposited by the petitioner in favour of the Gauhati High Court Bar Association within a period of 2 [two] weeks from today.

The instant writ petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking a direction for setting aside and quashing the notice bearing No.KRA.29/2021/01 dated 16.09.2021 issued by the respondent No.3 as well as also for a direction to the respondent authorities, more particularly, to the respondent Nos.2 & 3 to release the compensation amount of Rs.78,93,750/- being the compensation for acquisition of a plot of land owned by the petitioners measuring 2 bighas 10  lechas comprised in Dag No.184 (Pt) of Patta No.803 situated at village-Majirgaon, Mouza-Ramcharani under Azara Revenue Circle in the district of Kamrup (Metro), Assam.

opennyai_summary.17_August_2023__ANALYSIS:
5. Therefore, from the above dispute, it would be seen that the dispute falls within the ambit of the apportionment of the compensation.
From a perusal of the above Section, it would show that the Collector shall in every case where any person is aggrieved by an award made under Sub-Section (3) of Section 11 of the Act of 1964 or whether there is an disagreement with regard to the compensation payable on the application of the person entitled to compensation requiring the matter to be referred to Court, refer the matter to the decision of the Court.
Therefore, it was the bounden duty of the Collector that if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the said amount or any part thereof or as to the person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the Collector may refer such dispute to the decision Page No.# 5/5 of the Court.
Therefore, the dispute in the instant case as to who would be entitle the amount of Rs.78,93,750/- if cannot be settled by the Collector, the Collector or the Land Acquisition Officer so authorized has to refer the dispute to the Court.
7. Under such circumstances, it is the opinion of this Court that the said dispute so raised in the instant writ petition cannot be decided by this Court.
opennyai_summary.17_August_2023__decision:
However, taking into account the provision of Section 12 of the Act of 1964 read with Sections 18, 30 & 31 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act of 1894,
this Court gives liberty to the parties, if they have any dispute as regards the apportionment of the amount to file appropriate application before the Collector or the Land Acquisition Officer so entrusted with the acquisition proceedings pertaining to LA Case No.4/2018 thereby seeking a reference to the Court.
8. This Court further observes and directs, if such application is filed, the Collector and/or the Land Acquisition Officer, without any delay, shall refer the dispute to the Court for deciding the said dispute pertaining to apportionment.
It is further observed and directed that if disputes as regards apportionment cannot be resolved, the Collector/Land Acquisition Officer shall deposit the said amount in the Court.
9. With the above observation and direction, the instant petition stands disposed of.

During the said proceedings, no land document was produced by the petitioner to show that he was the owner of the said plot of land.

The writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 5060/2023 came up for consideration on 01.09.2023 and the same was disposed of with a direction to the respondent authorities to verify whether the land wherein the petitioner was in occupation had been included in the Notifications issued under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956 and if the said land had been included in the Notifications under Section 3A and Section 3D of the National Highways Act, 1956, then the respondent authorities would be at liberty to evict the petitioner from the said land.
When such facts were brought to light, the learned counsel for the petitioner made a submission on 06.09.2024, when the writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 1858/2024 was taken up for consideration, to the effect that since there were disputed questions of fact, he may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition, with a liberty to approach the competent court agitating the grievance as regards claim for zirat compensation in connection with the aforesaid plot of land.
submitted that since disputed questions of fact were involved, the petitioner be permitted to withdraw the writ petition with the liberty to approach the competent court.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments: 7. By this writ petition, the petitioner has sought to open up the litigation for the third occasion seeking inter alia a direction to the respondent authorities to assess the amount of zirat compensation in respect of the plot of land covered by Dag no. 363.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
It is, thus, clear that the competent court where the petitioner required to approach is not this Court exercising jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
The very reason for which the petitioner made the prayer to approach the competent court was involvement of disputed questions of facts.
8. It is well settled that a writ petition involving disputed questions of facts which require leading of evidence by the parties, is ordinarily not to be entertained.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Thus, it is clear that Page No.# 5/5 liberty granted to the petitioner vide Order dated 06.09.2024 cannot be a writ petition and as such,
this writ petition is not to be entertained.
The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed.
9. Despite order dated 06.09.2024, the petitioner has approached again without approaching the competent court of law.
Such an approach is clearly an abuse of the process and as such, the petitioner is imposed with a cost of Rs. 2,000/-, which sum is to be deposited by the petitioner in favour of the Gauhati High Court Bar Association within a period of 2 [two] weeks from today.
